is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus, a major malaria vector (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on several resistance markers including GSTe2 L119F, CYP6P9a-R, 6.5kb-SV, CYP9K1 G454A, and CPR N70I (page 2, 9, 10).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Figure 7 provides allele frequencies for multiple SNPs across different populations and years (page 11). Table S5 and S6 also contain genotype/allele frequency data.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Cameroon, Ghana, Uganda, and Malawi (page 15).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study using RNA-Seq, Pool-Seq, and transgenic expression (page 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific collection sites are provided: Mibellon (Cameroon), Tororo and Mayuge (Uganda), Atatam (Ghana), and Chikwawa (Malawi) (page 15).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study compares populations from 2014/2015 and 2021 (page 2, 15).

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the paper uses some previously published temporal data (Weedall et al. 2020), it presents new 2021 collections and new analyses (page 16).

supplement.evidence: The provided PDF includes the main text and figures; supplementary tables and figures are referenced and described in the text, and the study is self-contained for the purpose of this assessment.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the genomic drivers of pyrethroid resistance escalation in Anopheles funestus across four African countries (Cameroon, Ghana, Uganda, Malawi) between 2014 and 2021. It integrates RNA-Seq, Pool-Seq, and transgenic functional validation to identify key resistance genes and markers, including P450s, CPR (N70I), and structural variants.
